corrected_value.title: “I really liked that movie”: Testing the relationship between trait empathy, transportation, perceived realism, and movie enjoyment.

decisions.location: Discussion (lines 659-665); see also Introduction (lines 143-148), The Present Study (lines 209-210), Results (lines 389-413), and References (lines 872-875)
decisions.quote:
The correlation detected between trait empathy and narrative transportation supports and
extends prior literature that has demonstrated
similar results with films (Hall & Bracken, 2011;
Taylor, 2015), as well as studies that have examined
the relationship between some components of trait
empathy and narrative transportation into written
pieces (Bal & Veltkamp, 2013; Johnson, 2012).
decisions.reason: All three criteria for a genuine missing target are met: (1) the paper identifies the specific empirical finding of Hall and Bracken (2011) showing a positive correlation between multidimensional trait empathy and narrative transportation (lines 143-148), formulates Hypothesis 1 explicitly to test that correlation ('The first hypothesis was that trait empathy would be positively correlated with narrative transportation (Hall & Bracken, 2011; Taylor, 2015)', lines 209-210), empirically re-tests it in a new sample using the IRI and Narrative Transportation Scale in Results (r = .39, p < .001, lines 389-413), and in Discussion characterizes testing this relationship as its 'primary aim' (lines 640-642) and directly compares the observed correlation against Hall and Bracken (2011) (lines 659-662); (2) the reference list (lines 872-875) and verified Crossref metadata confirm the exact work: Hall, A. E., & Bracken, C. C. (2011), Journal of Media Psychology, 23(2), 90-99, DOI 10.1027/1864-1105/a000036; and (3) the sole shipped row (input_row_index '1577', doi_o '10.1016/j.poetic.2015.07.001') represents only Black and Barnes (2015a) (sibling blind target_index 0), an independent work testing genre differences on transportation. Prior adjudication and state files (7c6931f7...json and 44a1147d...json) are absent for this never-adjudicated work.
